_status: DERIVED, not measured on the repaired code. The GPU measurement job is scripts/autoinit/measure_causal_depth_runtime.py and is NOT authorized; this is what a budget decision can be made against, and what that job would confirm.
the_question: attempt 10 invalidated the 180-minute search assumption. Was the assumption wrong, or was the path wrong?
answer: the path. The frozen cost model's hardware calibration is itself a measurement of this exact workload on an accelerator, and the repair restores that path rather than inventing a new one.

frozen_cost_model_measurement.quote: E8a: 260 subset evaluations over a 67-item / 59,763-position mixture in 1,300 s at 4.02B full width
frozen_cost_model_measurement.hardware: L40S, $0.99/h, 88.83 effective TFLOP/s (~24.5% of bf16 peak)

independent_derivation.note: two independent routes to the same number is why this is offered as a bound rather than a guess

reduction_on_the_accelerator.note: the reduction is bandwidth-bound and small beside the forwards ONCE it is on the device. On the host it was the whole cost.

vram_bound.cache_gate: BUDGET_FRACTION 0.66 of free-after-model (~24.8 GiB) vs a 16.91 GiB cache -> ENABLED, so the (evals+1)*items cost structure holds and the fallback is not taken
vram_bound.caveat: excludes activations and allocator fragmentation; the measurement job reports the real peak

pricing_implication.search_minutes_180_status: NOT invalidated for the repaired path. It was invalidated for the host path. The beam-6 correction already carries the search to 216.2 min, which is the cost model's own beam-6 figure.
pricing_implication.recommended_next_step: measure before re-pricing: run scripts/autoinit/measure_causal_depth_runtime.py on one short L40S session (~2 min of evaluations plus teacher load) and compare evaluations/min against 12.0 and peak VRAM against 25.81 GiB.
pricing_implication.why_not_just_reprice_now: attempt 10 is the proof that a port can differ from its ancestor in ways no CPU run reveals. The derivation says the repaired code SHOULD hit E8a's rate; only the GPU says it DOES.

measurement_job.status: corrected and $0-executed; NOT authorized and NOT run on a GPU

sampling.scheme: skip(c, j) = {(3j + 5k) mod 36 : k < c}; RNG-free, recomputable by hand
sampling.why_stride_5: gcd(5,36)=1, so layers are distinct and spread across depth; a block of eight adjacent layers is neither representative nor equally costly

weighted_extrapolation.why: round r evaluates |skip|=r+1 over 36-r candidates, so larger skip sets run FEWER layers and are cheaper. Timing everything at cardinality 8 would overstate evaluations/min and understate the 260-evaluation runtime; the artifact reports that flat figure alongside, labelled WRONG, so the difference is visible

cost_ceiling_usd.basis: 24 timed evaluations + one production reference pass + 2 E8a paired checks with the reference RECOMPUTED (2 forwards/item/pair), plus 8 min teacher load, 12 min pod setup, 5 min overhead, then 3x
cost_ceiling_usd.note: E8a's cache_reference=False costs +0.08 min, so the recomputed 3x bound ($1.3571) sits UNDER the previously proposed $1.6294. The higher figure is retained as the hard ceiling because it is more conservative, not because it is needed.

memory_lifetime.problem: the job could hold TWO ~16.9 GiB accelerator reference caches at once - the production _ReferenceLogits cache still live while E8a built its own - which would either OOM the measurement or make the reported peak describe a dual-cache arrangement no Phase-A run has
fix: the production peak is read immediately after the timed evaluations, before anything else exists
the production cache is cleared and dropped (gc + empty_cache) before E8a's path is built
E8a runs with cache_reference=False: the pairs validate backend numerics, not E8a throughput, and E8a defines recomputation as numerically identical
both peaks are reported, distinctly; production_peak_gib is the Phase-A number and the comparison peak is never substituted for it
memory_lifetime.safe_because: the port's per-item results are already scalars (DistortionSums.as_dict()), so releasing the cache loses nothing still needed - and a test fails if they ever become tensors
memory_lifetime.e8a_pairs: explicit and deterministic: one |skip|=1 and one |skip|=8, which bracket the schedule. Not the first two dict entries. The count was NOT increased.
